You are a subagent spawned by another session.
Design Phase E7 (Solana A+ Touch) of the Financial Resilience Engine in "/Users/ajeet/Projects/Hackathons/Sheridan Datathon 2026". Design/review only, do NOT write files (deliver content for the orchestrator to land). A concurrent agent implements E6 (judge/, App.tsx, ConsoleView one line, consoleStore comment, public/judge-sheet.html): read for context only, never design changes to those beyond the one integration seam you must specify (where the receipt badge mounts).

## Phase E7 scope (approved plan)
"E7 Solana A+ touch (gated): memo package + honest receipt badge in the verdict card." This is the user-approved "A+ light touch": the decoupled static memo anchor (per the approved gated package in docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md) PLUS a small honest badge in the engine's verdict card linking to the bundled chain receipt. Badge copy must pass the deception test: reads as a bundled receipt, never as a live on-chain write. ZERO runtime RPC. Network allowed but never required.

## Context to read first
- docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md (the APPROVED gated package: three receipts — findings.json root memo, model_card.json hash, F1 aggregate fingerprint; static chain-receipt panel; nine-check acceptance bar; the gated conditions: root memo confirmed, findings re-run green, 60 minute cap, paid from cut-order budget, gate failure -> ship single memo silently)
- docs/solana.md (report footer wording contract: "Anchored on Solana devnet, verified" / "anchored at build time, signature: <sig>" / "no evidence yet" — ReceiptBadge already pins these)
- src/components/judge/ReceiptBadge.tsx + test (scaffold verdict KEEP: three states, exact wording from docs/solana.md, props-only, zero network, honest placeholder when evidence missing; currently ORPHANED, nothing mounts it)
- scripts/solana/send_memo.py + evidence layout (scripts/solana/evidence/, bundled under public/data/)
- What evidence artifacts currently exist: check public/data/ for memo-devnet*.json (root memo was already sent in a prior session per docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md "already run; this receipt is the gate"); check scripts/solana/evidence/
- src/components/console/VerdictBadge.tsx / ShockPanel (E2) — candidate mount point for "the verdict card"; E6 is concurrently touching judge/ and App.tsx — specify the mount point carefully to minimize collision (E6 brief says JudgeBar may gain a receipt link slot later)
- The E1 artifact meta has sources sha256 and profiles.json SHA256 from verify.py (possible receipt material: anchor the artifact hash?)
- docs/competition-day-runbook.md Phase 6 (receipts and panel) and Phase 9 (future-work paragraph) — the execution plan already written there

## Design questions to settle
1. Scope reconciliation: the original gated package was designed for the OLD findings-first site (three receipts + a static panel in "section E"). Under the full pivot, what remains meaningful? Recommend: which receipts to ship now (root memo already sent; model_card/F1 fingerprint relate to dropped findings surfaces but the findings machinery still exists in-repo), whether to add a receipts-of-the-engine artifact (profiles.json SHA256 as a fourth receipt?) or keep strictly to the approved three, and where the "static chain-receipt panel" lives in the new single-page layout (a small section? inside the judge sheet? a footer block?). Respect the 60 minute cap and the gate-failure rule.
2. Badge mount: exact component and props for the "honest receipt badge in the verdict card" (VerdictBadge? BaselineCard? a footer? JudgeBar slot reserved by E6?). Consider the E6 collision surface and pick the lowest-conflict mount; specify the exact props (evidence object shape, link target, base-path-aware URL).
3. Evidence flow: what files land under public/data/ (bundled JSON only), how the badge reads them (static import vs fetch of bundled json — note the offline rule: static import of a small JSON is fine and avoids fetch), and how honesty is guaranteed (badge states the receipt was anchored at build time with signature, links to the bundled evidence file and/or Solana explorer URL ONLY as a hyperlink, never as a fetch).
4. Gating: E7 is explicitly GATED. Define the gate conditions adapted from the approved package (evidence files exist and verify? root memo confirmed? 60 min cap? what happens if a receipt is missing: badge renders the honest "no evidence yet" placeholder — is that an acceptable ship state?) and the cut rule if time runs short (badge ships placeholder, panel omitted, write-up paragraph still lands?).
5. The write-up paragraph: the approved exact sentence in docs/ideas-tangerine-solana.md Phase 9 (future work, labeled not-built) — confirm it still applies under the pivot (F3 AUC 0.590 reference) and where it goes (docs/devpost.md is owned by another session — specify the sentence and target so the orchestrator can route it).
6. MLH Solana track claim: what specifically earns the track under the light touch (the devnet memo + visible receipt surface + honest write-up) and what the booth Q&A one-liner is (the rejection rationale line already written).
7. Test plan + ordered implementation steps (~1 hour, gated) + acceptance checklist (adapt the nine checks) + risks.

If you need clarification or encounter ambiguity, output your questions in this exact format at the TOP of your response with recommended defaults:

## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: [your question]

Then continue with your best-effort output based on available information.

Output: component/file breakdown with exact paths, evidence flow diagram, badge mount decision, gate conditions, ordered steps, acceptance checklist, risks, plus ready-to-land docs/architecture.md + docs/decisions.md content.

1: # Tangerine x Solana bridge concepts: assessment
2: 
3: Date: Nov 07 2026
4: Status: approved outcome at top; one gated micro-addition approved, every other concept rejected (verdict table below).
5: 
6: ## Approved outcome (top)
7: 
8: Approved: one gated package attached to the existing Solana memo anchor. Three receipts (findings.json root memo, model_card.json hash, F1 aggregate fingerprint), a static chain-receipt panel in section E reading bundled evidence, and one explicitly labeled not-built future-work paragraph in the write-up. Gate conditions, acceptance bar, and the rejection rationale are in the sections below. Execution lives in docs/competition-day-runbook.md Phase 6 (receipts and panel) and Phase 9 (paragraph); the decision record is docs/decisions.md, Nov 07 2026.
9: 
10: Everything else from the concept round is rejected. No wallet UI, no Anchor, no tokens, no 3D, no runtime RPC.
11: 
12: ## Context
13: 
14: External advice proposed bridging Tangerine banking data with Solana via behavioral credit scoring, yield streaming, dual-layer dashboards, and a risk-shield particle field. Two independent assessments (planner plus product manager) adjudicated them against the locked plan (docs/decisions.md, Nov 06 LOCKED: memo anchor only, hard stop Sat 5:30 PM).
15: 
16: ## Concept verdict table
17: 
18: | Concept | Source | Verdict | Cost / scope | Reason |
19: |---------|--------|---------|--------------|--------|
20: | SolCash credit line | external | REJECTED | 8 to 14 hours, Anchor | violates the locked program, token, wallet, and oracle scopes; Data Use self-own since F3 AUC 0.590 contradicts credit gating; optics at bank sponsor event |
21: | Yield streamer | external | REJECTED | 6 to 12 hours, Anchor | runtime scheduler breaks offline booth; nonexistent yield |
22: | Dual-layer dashboard, live version | external | REJECTED | wallet UI plus runtime RPC | both are scope violations; runtime RPC dies offline |
23: | Dual-layer static receipt panel | external | ACCEPTED (micro-addition) | reads bundled JSON only | honest static proof surface, zero runtime calls |
24: | Risk-shield particle field | external | REJECTED | 3D cancelled; second hero viz | liquidation theater implies mechanisms that do not run |
25: | Fake-oracle framing | external | REJECTED | deceptive framing | the devnet-only half already shipped as the memo anchor |
26: | Per-finding attestation set G | planner addition | ACCEPTED (gated) | inside the 60 minute cap | receipts over new mechanisms |
27: | F1 fingerprint proof K | planner addition | ACCEPTED (gated) | inside the 60 minute cap | aggregates only, no raw rows |
28: | Payday schedule commitment H | planner addition | not accepted today | not part of the gated package | no gate conditions prepared |
29: | Escrow pledge I | planner addition | not accepted today (memo version); Anchor version = future work | Anchor is out of scope today | post-event weekend project, see Future work |
30: | Resilience reputation J | planner addition | REJECTED | identity and oracle implications | breaks the no identity, no oracle scope locks |
31: | Streaks/duels L | planner addition | REJECTED | game layer mechanic | rejected at assessment; not part of the gated package |
32: 
33: ## Key insight
34: 
35: The instinct behind the concepts is already the shipped memo anchor: put a durable, checkable claim next to the analysis. The heavier versions are the same plan at 10x risk and hours. The gated package keeps the instinct and drops the weight.
36: 
37: ## Approved gated package (exact conditions)
38: 
39: Conditions, all required, identical across docs/competition-day-runbook.md Phase 6 and docs/decisions.md:
40: 
41: 1. Root memo confirmed by the 4:30 PM decision line (5:30 PM death line, unchanged).
42: 2. Findings re-run verified green first (Phase 4: verify_findings and pytest exit 0).
43: 3. 60 minute cap on the whole gated package.
44: 4. Paid from cut-order items: devnet stone (cut 2) and motion accents (cut 3), never from new budget.
45: 5. Gate failure at any point: ship the single memo, skip silently (no panel, no paragraph).
46: 
47: Deliverables, all inside the cap:
48: 
49: 1. Three receipts, all sent with `scripts/solana/send_memo.py --file`, evidence as sibling files under `scripts/solana/evidence/` and bundled under `public/data/`:
50:    - findings.json root memo: `memo-devnet.json` (already run; this receipt is the gate).
51:    - model_card.json hash: `memo-devnet-modelcard.json`.
52:    - F1 aggregate fingerprint: SHA256 over the published F1 aggregate table (`f1StructuralVsDiscretionary` in findings.json), with the note "aggregates only, no raw rows" in the memo prefix: `memo-devnet-fingerprint.json`.
53: 2. Static chain-receipt panel in section E reading the bundled `public/data/memo-devnet.json` plus the two new evidence files (`public/data/memo-devnet-modelcard.json`, `public/data/memo-devnet-fingerprint.json`). No runtime RPC, no network calls.
54: 3. One explicitly-labeled-not-built future-work paragraph in the write-up (Phase 9), exact sentence:
55: 
56:    > future work: a behavioral score attested on chain could gate a credit line or automate surplus sweeps; not implemented, and the underlying model (F3, AUC 0.590) is not strong enough to gate credit
57: 
58: ## Acceptance bar (nine checks, from the assessment)
59: 
60: - [ ] ships by 4:30 PM
61: - [ ] zero new runtime network calls
62: - [ ] zero scope violations (no wallet UI, no Anchor, no tokens, no 3D, no runtime RPC)
63: - [ ] consumes only bundled artifacts
64: - [ ] every number matches findings.json
65: - [ ] deception test (no product language for mechanisms that do not run, simulated labeled on surface)
66: - [ ] single-story test
67: - [ ] cut-first rule
68: - [ ] zero video budget impact
69: 
70: ## Rejection rationale (booth Q&A one-liner)
71: 
72: > we anchored the findings themselves on chain because that is the claim that needed the chain; everything else stayed on the honest side of the line.
73: 
74: ## Future work (post-event weekend projects)
75: 
76: - SolCash credit line: behavioral score gating a credit line (Anchor program, wallet UI). Blocked today by scope locks and by F3 (AUC 0.590) not being strong enough to gate credit.
77: - Yield streamer: needs a runtime scheduler and an on chain yield source; breaks the offline booth and there is no real yield to stream.
78: - Escrow pledge, Anchor version: the memo version was not accepted today; the program version is a weekend build after the event.

1: # Solana devnet memo anchor runbook
2: 
3: Dated: Nov 06 2026 (proof run), commands below are for Saturday Nov 07 2026.
4: 
5: Scope (docs/decisions.md, Nov 06 LOCKED): memo anchor ONLY. The report footer
6: shows a Solana devnet receipt for the SHA256 of findings.json. No wallet UI,
7: no Anchor program, no tokens. Devnet only, no real funds, no financial data
8: on chain.
9: 
10: ## Safety rails (always on)
11: 
12: - Agave CLI is not on PATH. Every shell command starts with:
13:   `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/solana/install/active_release/bin:$PATH"`
14: - Config is on devnet (RPC https://api.devnet.solana.com).
15: - Keypair lives at `~/.config/solana/id.json`, mode 600, outside the repo.
16:   Never overwrite it, never commit it. `.gitignore` covers `id.json`,
17:   `*-keypair.json`, and both patterns under `scripts/solana/`.
18: - `scripts/solana/send_memo.py` refuses to sign until the endpoint's genesis
19:   hash equals the known devnet genesis
20:   `REDACTED`. Fail closed on mismatch.
21: - Memo program on devnet: `REDACTED`
22:   (verified executable via getAccountInfo on Nov 06 2026). The id
23:   `REDACTED` that circulated in planning
24:   notes fails base58 decode (WrongSize) and is wrong.
25: 
26: ## Faucet rule
27: 
28: AI agents must not use web faucets (faucet.solana.com needs a human sign in).
29: Funding order for agents:
30: 
31: 1. `solana airdrop 2 "$(solana address)" --url devnet` (the user-authoritative
32:    CLI faucet).
33: 2. Proof of Work fallback:
34:    `cargo install devnet-pow` once, then
35:    `devnet-pow mine -d 3 --reward 0.02 --no-infer -t 5000000000`.
36:    Note: devnet-pow's claim path also calls requestAirdrop, so it fails with
37:    the same error while the faucet is closed, and it needs 5000 lamports of
38:    fee already in the wallet when the faucet is open.
39: 3. `solana-test-validator` plus a local airdrop only proves the send path
40:    locally (see `scripts/solana/localnet_selftest.py`). Local SOL never
41:    reaches devnet.
42: 4. If all agent paths fail, a human operator may fund the wallet once at
43:    https://faucet.solana.com. Reference:
44:    https://solana.com/developers/cookbook/development/airdrops-and-faucets
45: 
46: Observed Nov 06 2026, 21:00 EDT (both agent paths closed):
47: 
48: | Route | Result |
49: |-------|--------|
50: | `solana airdrop 2 ... --url devnet` | `Error: airdrop request failed. This can happen when the rate limit is reached.` exit 1 |
51: | Raw `requestAirdrop` RPC | HTTP 410, `{"code":410,"message":"The RPC faucet is closed on this cluster. Request test SOL at https://faucet.solana.com"}` |
52: | `devnet-pow mine -d 3 --reward 0.02 --no-infer -t 5000000000` | `Error: airdrop request failed.` exit 1 (same closed faucet) |
53: | `solana airdrop 1 ... --url devnet` retry | same error, balance stayed 0 SOL |
54: 
55: ## Saturday Nov 07 exact commands
56: 
57: Step 1, toolchain and funding:
58: 
59: ```bash
60: export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/solana/install/active_release/bin:$PATH"
61: solana --version            # expect solana-cli 4.3.2
62: solana address              # expect REDACTED
63: solana airdrop 2 "$(solana address)" --url devnet
64: solana balance              # must be > 0 before the send
65: ```
66: 
67: If the airdrop still fails with error 410, run the PoW fallback from the
68: faucet rule section, then check the balance again. If both fail, ask the human
69: operator to fund once at faucet.solana.com. Do not proceed without a balance
70: above 5000 lamports.
71: 
72: Step 2, hash the frozen findings file and send one memo transaction:
73: 
74: ```bash
75: cd "/Users/ajeet/Projects/Hackathons/Sheridan Datathon 2026"
76: shasum -a 256 public/data/findings.json   # record this digest in the notes
77: uv run --with solders==0.29.0 python scripts/solana/send_memo.py \
78:     --file public/data/findings.json \
79:     --prefix "Sheridan Datathon 2026 findings.json" \
80:     --evidence scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet.json
81: ```
82: 
83: The script prints the signature, confirms it, reads the memo back from chain,
84: verifies the on chain text matches, and writes the evidence file. For a smoke
85: test before the real file, the payload is the SHA256 of the string
86: `Ledger Odyssey test`:
87: 
88: ```bash
89: uv run --with solders==0.29.0 python scripts/solana/send_memo.py \
90:     --text "Ledger Odyssey test" \
91:     --evidence scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet.json
92: ```
93: 
94: Known digest of that test string (verified Nov 06 2026):
95: `bac6b28265843eb4a276198eb3ab9337de1d27e33a4a2e872b142196865473c5`
96: 
97: Step 3, confirm independently and capture the explorer link:
98: 
99: ```bash
100: export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/solana/install/active_release/bin:$PATH"
101: solana confirm <SIG> --url devnet
102: # Explorer URL (also written into the evidence file):
103: # https://explorer.solana.com/tx/<SIG>?cluster=devnet
104: ```
105: 
106: Step 4, copy the committable evidence next to the other public fixtures:
107: 
108: ```bash
109: cp scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet.json public/data/memo-devnet.json
110: ```
111: 
112: Evidence file schema (committable, contains no secrets):
113: `signature`, `slot`, `payload_sha256`, `cluster` ("devnet"), `program_id`,
114: `rpc`, `confirmed_at`, `explorer_url`, plus supporting fields
115: (`confirmation_status`, `block_time`, `signer_pubkey`, `payload`,
116: `memo_text_on_chain`, `matches_local`).
117: 
118: ## Report footer wording
119: 
120: Verified case (RPC read-back succeeded at build time):
121: 
122: > Anchored on Solana devnet, verified
123: 
124: Offline fallback (RPC unreachable, or read-back skipped):
125: 
126: > anchored at build time, signature: <sig>
127: 
128: with `<sig>` replaced by the transaction signature from the bundled evidence
129: file.
130: 
131: Build-time-bundled-evidence recommendation: copy
132: `scripts/solana/evidence/memo-devnet.json` to `public/data/memo-devnet.json`
133: before `npm run build` and have the footer read signature, digest, and
134: explorer link from that bundled file. Do not fetch the devnet RPC from the
135: browser at runtime in production: the public endpoint is rate limited per IP
136: (100 requests per 10 seconds documented, plus per method and per second
137: headers) and an offline judge would see a broken footer. The bundled file is
138: the source of truth; a live read-back is a verification step, not a runtime
139: dependency.
140: 
141: ## RPC read-back and limits
142: 
143: Read-back against https://api.devnet.solana.com (verified Nov 06 2026 with a
144: live memo transaction):
145: 
146: | Method | Result |
147: |--------|--------|
148: | `getTransaction` (encoding jsonParsed) | works, returns the `spl-memo` instruction with parsed text and program id |
149: | `getParsedTransaction` | disabled, error `-32601 Method not found` |
150: | `getSignatureStatuses` | works, returns `confirmationStatus`, `err`, `slot` |
151: | `sendTransaction` | used by the script with base64 encoding |
152: 
153: CORS check with `Origin: http://localhost:5173`:
154: 
155: - Preflight `OPTIONS` returns `access-control-allow-origin:
156:   http://localhost:5173`, `access-control-allow-methods: OPTIONS, POST, GET`,
157:   `access-control-allow-headers: authorization, content-type`.
158: - Actual `POST` also returns `access-control-allow-origin:
159:   http://localhost:5173` (the header is reflected for allowed origins).
160: - So browser read-back from the Vite dev server works today. Production
161:   still uses the bundled evidence file, for the rate limit reasons above.
162: 
163: Limits: the public devnet endpoint documents 100 requests per 10 seconds per
164: IP. Observed response headers on the free tier also advertise per method and
165: per second caps (`x-ratelimit-rps-limit: 250`, `x-ratelimit-method-limit:
166: 150` on `getVersion`). Treat the endpoint as scarce: one read-back per build,
167: no polling loops from the page.
168: 
169: ## Hard stop and drop track
170: 
171: Saturday Nov 07 5:30 PM local is the hard stop for the Solana item
172: (docs/decisions.md). If the memo transaction is not confirmed with an
173: explorer link by then, drop the Solana track claim from the submission and
174: ship the report without the anchor footer. Do not spend time past the stop
175: on faucet retries; the drop-track rule wins.
176: 
177: ## Verification status of the Nov 06 proof run
178: 
179: | Step | Status |
180: |------|--------|
181: | CLI 4.3.2, devnet config, keypair mode 600 | done |
182: | Airdrop (CLI, then PoW) | blocked, faucet closed (error 410), balance 0 SOL |
183: | Memo program id check on devnet | done, executable, script id confirmed |
184: | send_memo.py devnet mode | verified up to the funding gate (genesis assertion, signer, digest all pass) |
185: | Confirm, evidence file, read-back of our own tx | pending funding, first task Saturday |
186: | Localnet selftest | available as offline proof of the send path |
187: | Key material grep over scripts/solana/ | clean, no base58 secrets, no key arrays, no id.json tracked |

1: # Financial Resilience Engine Architecture
2: 
3: Last updated: Sat Nov 07 2026 (Phase E1 complete).
4: Status: E1 profile precompute shipped and verified. E2 console base
5: next.
6: 
7: ## Product
8: 
9: A financial resilience engine for real bank customers, built for the
10: Tangerine track of the Sheridan Datathon 2026. At judging a judge picks
11: an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five
12: minutes:
13: 
14: 1. **Know the customer.** Any account shows typical income I, fixed
15:    costs F, spending S, savings buffer B, household bills H, loan
16:    payment P, gap, and months of runway, all from the precomputed
17:    profile artifact.
18: 2. **Take a shock.** A shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up
19:    15 percent, a one-off repair, or a mix) changes income or spending
20:    and the runway recomputes with the judge's branch rules.
21: 3. **Make a plan.** A goal plan (emergency fund) and a backup plan
22:    (if the shock lands) built from the same numbers.
23: 
24: The engine is the primary demo surface (full pivot, approved Nov 07
25: 2026). The orbit game and the findings first report framing are dropped
26: as surfaces; their machinery (F1 structural and discretionary spend, F5
27: ranked interventions, BalanceRiver canvas, provenance stamps) may be
28: reused internally inside the engine. Every number a judge sees traces
29: back to source rows through provenance checksums.
30: 
31: ## Hard constraints
32: 
33: - **Judge definitions are the contract.** I, F, S, B, H, P and the
34:   runway come from docs/tangerine-challenge.md. Any deviation must be
35:   deliberate, documented in docs/decisions.md, and explainable to a
36:   judge.
37: - **Integer cents end to end.** Dollars convert with
38:   `np.rint(dollars * 100)` once at load; every metric, mean, median and
39:   runway division afterwards is integer arithmetic with ROUND_HALF_UP
40:   (ties away from zero). No float may decide a branch.
41: - **Deterministic offline artifact.** profiles.json carries no
42:   timestamps, no randomness, and no floats; two consecutive builds are
43:   byte identical. All data is bundled for an offline booth.
44: - **Checksummed sources fail loud.** The three canonical CSVs are
45:   verified against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before any row is read.
46: - **Any account must work.** All 4500 accounts, including the five edge
47:   flags (pensioner, thin history, zero income, defaulted loan, negative
48:   buffer), must render without a special case.
49: - **Content convention:** no em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double
50:   hyphens, or spaced hyphens in shipped strings. verify.py scans the
51:   artifact and exits non zero on a violation.
52: - **Static hosting only.** GitHub Pages, no server, no runtime network
53:   calls beyond bundled assets.
54: 
55: ## Stack
56: 
57: - Python 3.14 + uv + pandas + numpy for the offline engine pipeline;
58:   pytest for tests. Modules are header-style, snake_case, type hinted.

197: alongside Tangerine, Entire, Solana, and GoDaddy.
198: 
199: ### Request shape
200: 
201: - Plain fetch to
202:   https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent
203:   with the x-goog-api-key header. No SDK: the newer JS client sends an
204:   Api-Revision header that fails CORS preflight with 403.
205: - Model gemini-3.5-flash-lite or 3.6-flash with thinkingLevel minimal
206:   and store false. store true adds about 2.7 seconds; 3.8 Flash
207:   thinking can take 10 to 25 seconds.
208: - Structured output: responseMimeType application/json with a strict
209:   responseSchema, all fields required, additionalProperties false. The
210:   schema returns intent (enum job_loss, bills_up, one_off_cost, mixed,
211:   no_shock), incomeFactor (number 0 to 1), billsPct (number 0 to 1),
212:   oneOffMonths (number 0 to 12), durationMonths (integer 0 to 120,
213:   display only), confidence (enum high, medium, low), and summary
214:   (string, at most 90 characters).
215: - Prompt payload (user decision, recorded honestly): the request
216:   carries the twist sentence, the account_id string, and the account's
217:   six judge baseline metrics as plain numbers (I, F, S, B, H, P and
218:   baseline runway). It does not carry raw rows, transaction history, or
219:   any other customer data. The competition privacy rule is respected
220:   at the row level; the account identifier and aggregate metrics do
221:   leave the browser, which the user explicitly approved on Nov 07
222:   2026.
223: 
224: ### Shared ShockSpec
225: 
226: Exactly three math fields (incomeFactor, billsPct, oneOffMonths) plus
227: display only durationMonths. They map one to one onto the judge
228: formula: income_after = incomeFactor x I, spending_after = S + billsPct
229: x H, one_off_costs = oneOffMonths x S. Preset twist cards produce the
230: same ShockSpec, so one consumer handles both the typed path and the
231: preset path.
232: 
233: ### Validation before state change
234: 
235: TypeScript validation runs before any state change:
236: 
237: 1. JSON.parse in try/catch, then a hand written type guard (no zod; the
238:    repo uses pure functions plus vitest).
239: 2. Percent detection: if a value is greater than 1 and at most 100,
240:    divide by 100 and flag autoCorrected.
241: 3. Clamping to the schema ranges, flagged when clamped.
242: 4. Rounding for display: incomeFactor 2 dp, billsPct 2 dp, oneOffMonths
243:    1 dp.
244: 5. Reject to fallback when intent is no_shock, confidence is low, or
245:    every field sits at its neutral value (1, 0, 0).
246: 
247: ### Confirmation before apply
248: 
249: Nothing writes to app state until the presenter confirms the parsed
250: chips with one explicit click or Enter. The chips show each parameter
251: with a one click stepper for correction, plus a formula strip showing
252: income and spending in dollars so the presenter can verify against the
253: judge's hand calculation. The runway number does not exist until
254: confirmation. This is mandatory, not polish: a misparse visible to a
255: judge computing by hand is the worst failure mode.
256: 
257: ### Failure mode and timeout
258: 
259: - Timeout is AbortSignal.timeout(3000), a hard 3 seconds, then
260:   automatic fallback to preset cards.
261: - Preset twist cards are always rendered and always clickable. A mode
262:   badge next to the input reads "typed shock Gemini" or "preset
263:   cards".
264: - On 429, 403, abort, or network error: no retry on 429, an inline
265:   note reads "Gemini unavailable, using preset cards", the storm
266:   animation continues into the preset apply, and total delay stays
267:   under 3 seconds. The mode badge keeps showing the origin of the
268:   shock that is currently applied (user decision Nov 07 2026): a
269:   later failed parse does not relabel an applied Gemini shock as
270:   preset. The note alone reports the failed attempt.
271: - A hash cache makes repeated identical sentences free.
272: 
273: ### Key management
274: 
275: The key is already created with $25 of credits on the paid tier, so
276: free tier quota limits do not apply and content is not used for
277: product improvement under paid terms. It is stored as
278: import.meta.env.VITE_GEMINI_KEY, inlined into the bundle as expected
279: for a static site, never in a file under public/, and never printed in
280: the UI. HTTP referrer restriction is recommended: github.io, localhost,
281: and the final custom domain. Delete the key after Sunday submission.
282: 
283: ### UX timing budget (3 minute live twist)
284: 
285: The input row sits directly above the preset twist cards, labeled "Say
286: the shock". The storm front rolling in is the loading state (no
287: spinner, label "reading the sky"). Target latency is about 1 second,
288: hard cap 3 seconds. Stretch after P0 ships: the judge speaks the shock
289: via the browser Web Speech API at no extra API cost.
290: 
291: ### Effort and testing
292: 
293: - Core effort 5.5 to 7.5 hours: parser module 1.5 to 2, UI input row
294:   and chips 2 to 2.5, loading state 0.5 to 1, tests 1, key setup and
295:   smoke test 0.5 to 1. Stretch mic input adds 1 to 1.5 hours.
296: - Testing: vitest for the clamp table, percent detection, fallback on
297:   429 and abort, and the chip correction path, with mocked fetch. Log
298:   every response (sentence hash, latency ms, raw JSON, clamped JSON)
299:   to console.info so the write-up can quote a measured p50.
300: 
301: ### Fit with hard constraints
302: 
303: This is the "network allowed as a bonus, never a dependency" pattern
304: made concrete: the console is fully usable offline with preset cards,
305: and the typed path is the only code that touches the network. The
306: Gemini path reuses the E2 shock math unchanged, so the judge
307: definitions contract and the integer cents rule are untouched, and a
308: misparse can never reach state without the confirmation step.
309: 
310: ### Implementation layout
311: 
312: - Files: src/lib/shockParse.ts with shockParse.test.ts and
313:   shockParse.dash.test.ts; src/components/console/TypedShock.tsx and
314:   ShockChips.tsx with typedShock.smoke.test.ts; the consoleStore typed
315:   slice with consoleStore.typed.test.ts; the cp- block in src/index.css;
316:   and .env.example plus the .env rules appended to .gitignore.
317: - Typed boundary: parseShockSentence returns one union (ok, rejected,
318:   timeout) and shockSpecToTwist converts the confirmed spec, so the
319:   preset path and the typed path converge on one Twist consumer and one
320:   runway formula.
321: - Confirmation model: pendingShock never writes twist, so the runway
322:   cannot move until confirmTypedShock runs; the chips step through
323:   applySpecStep, the formula strip shows income and spending in
324:   dollars, and the confirm button is auto focused.
325: - Failure model: each reject reason maps to one fallback note, the
326:   mode badge always shows the origin of the applied shock rather than
327:   flipping on a failed parse (user decision Nov 07 2026), and the
328:   sentence hash cache is namespaced by account id because a one off
329:   cost converts through that account's spending.
